maria-support: Heads up — customer tenant_acme_42 reported a sudden spike in 429s and a billing surge after a token rotation last night. Route = /v1/generate, model = gpt-redwood-2-small. Example req id: req_7f3a2. Need quick obs pointers and a short repro so we can confirm whether this is a burst/quota misattribution or client retries hitting limits.
Sam (eng-sre): Can you paste the full request-id header and a sample curl? Also when did the token rotation happen? :eyes:
maria-support: rotation at 2026-03-16T22:11Z. Header we got in support logs: `X-Request-Id: req_7f3a2`, `X-Tenant: tenant_acme_42`. Minimal curl we captured: ```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <REPLACED>" 
 -H "X-Request-Id: req_7f3a2" 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-2-small","input":"hi"}'
```
Priya (support): They also got a bunch of 401s ~22:10Z before the 429s. Customer says their client immediately retried without exponential backoff. Could be 401 -> rotate -> replay burst.
Kai (eng-platform): For observability quick checks: run this aggregation in the internal query console to attribute 429s by tenant + route + model: ```sql
SELECT count(*) as errors, sum(tokens) as tokens_processed
FROM requests
WHERE status = 429 AND timestamp >= now() - interval '1 hour'
GROUP BY tenant_id, route, model
ORDER BY errors DESC
```
That will show whether the spikes are concentrated on tenant_acme_42 and /v1/generate. Also check `request_attempt` tag to see retries.
Anita-ops: On the Console: Observability -> Rate Limits -> Per-tenant view -> search tenant_acme_42. The timeline will show 429 spikes and associated quota windows. Also check the "burst window" metric for dev-facing Dedicated pools.
Sam (eng-sre): If you can, paste a short sample of the raw log lines around req_7f3a2. We want the client ip, user-agent, and any retry headers like `X-Retry-Count`. We should also look for repeated `Authorization` header changes.
maria-support: raw log snippet: ```
2026-03-16T22:10:59Z INFO req=req_7f3a1 tenant=tenant_acme_42 status=401 ua="acme-client/1.2"
2026-03-16T22:11:01Z INFO req=req_7f3a2 tenant=tenant_acme_42 status=429 ua="acme-client/1.2" retry_count=3
2026-03-16T22:11:02Z INFO req=req_7f3a3 tenant=tenant_acme_42 status=429 ua="acme-client/1.2" retry_count=4
```
Priya (support): That `retry_count` is the smoking gun. Client retried aggressively after 401. They also hit a short quota window because their project has a conservative burst allowance.
Kai (eng-platform): Repro steps we usually give customers: 1) Rotate token locally. 2) Disable backoff in the client. 3) Fire a controlled burst: ```bash
for i in {1..80}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN" -H "X-Request-Id: repro_$i" -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-2-small","input":"x"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done; wait
```
If that produces many 429s within a minute, it reproduces the burst behavior.
Anita-ops: Short-term mitigations: - Ask customer to enable client backoff and jitter. - Increase burst allowance for the tenant (if on Dedicated/reserved plan) or advise rate-limiting on client side. - In Console, create an alert: `tenant_429_rate > 50/min for 3m`.
Sam (eng-sre): Long-term: add tenant tag to the rate-limit dashboards so producers can click through from a 429 spike to the tenant billing usage and request samples. Also we should add an internal alert that links to the playbook runbook.
maria-support: Billing team flagged a spike of +$120 in token costs during the event. Is there a recommended billing attribution query?
Kai (eng-platform): Yes — in Billing -> Usage Explorer run: ```sql
SELECT sum(cost_usd) AS cost, count(*) AS requests
FROM requests
WHERE tenant_id = 'tenant_acme_42' AND timestamp BETWEEN '2026-03-16T22:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-16T22:15:00Z'
GROUP BY model, route
ORDER BY cost DESC
```
That ties cost to the route/model that produced the spike.
Priya (support): Next steps assigned: Sam to add tenant filter to RL dashboards (ETA 2d), Kai to add a short repro runbook link in Console (ETA 1d), support to send the controlled repro instructions to customer and confirm client backoff changes (today).
Sam (eng-sre): I'll also add a quick alert: "unexpected 429 burst by tenant" -> page on pagerduty if >100/min for 5m.
maria-support: Nice. One more ask — can we add the `X-Tenant` header into the logs we ship to S3 for faster cost audits? Right now it's only in the structured request table.
Anita-ops: Will take that to infra backlog — sounds reasonable.
ingest-bot: Automated note: ticket #SUP-8923 linked, billing analyzer attached.
Priya (support): Thanks team :thumbsup: We'll follow up after repro.
Sam (eng-sre): ack. Closing thread once repro confirmed. :white_check_mark:
